title: Indonesia hit by second powerful earthquake in one day as death toll rises to 47
facts: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Indonesia's Flores island killed at least 47 people.
Rescue official Fathur Rahman reported that 50 people were injured in the Flores earthquake.
Suharyanto leads Indonesia's national disaster management agency (BNPB).
The earthquake on Flores damaged nearly 160 houses along with educational and health facilities.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies organized emergency aid for 2,000 displaced people.
The Indonesian government dispatched 50,000 aid packages weighing 275 tonnes to Flores.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen offered assistance using Copernicus Earth observation satellites.
The 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Flores at approximately 5:30 a.m. local time.
Landslides triggered by the earthquake blocked roadways across Flores island.
Indonesia's BMKG geological agency recorded coastal waves of up to 1.6 meters in Flores.
The strongest recorded aftershock on Flores measured magnitude 6.1.
A second earthquake measuring magnitude 6.9 occurred near Pematangsiantar on Sumatra island.
The magnitude 6.9 Sumatra earthquake struck roughly 12 hours after the Flores event.
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake and subsequent tsunami in Flores killed approximately 2,500 people in 1992.
A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra in 2004 triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 people across the region.
